note: Extracted from docs/DECISIONS.md §4.4. The vocabulary decision is the one place in this project where a design choice has a price attached end to end.

buys.note: Indic fertility from about 2.4 to about 1.85 tokens per word.

over.note: The India slice of a 15T budget.

vocab_trade.return: Roughly a 5x return on the 1.2% compute cost, for one epoch, before any inference-side saving.

run_cost.note: Recomputed by dataframework/run_cost.py from the budget the page recommends, using the three constants docs/DECISIONS.md 4.4 already uses: 6ND for training FLOPs, 4.0e14 sustained FLOP/s per H100, and that section's own USD/INR rate. It shipped as a static block worked against a 15T budget and stayed there when the recommendation moved to 16.8T, which made it 12% low.
run_cost.caveat: Compute only, and one full pass of the schedule. It excludes data acquisition, annotation, storage, egress, the failed runs every real project has, and every salary. A published rate of USD 2.00 per H100-hour is a list price; large reservations are negotiated well below it and spot capacity below that again. Treat it as the order of magnitude, which is what the fork actually turns on.

provenance.note: Everything here is derived, and every derivation is shown as ordered steps so it can be checked. The one exception is called out: the fertility improvement a larger vocabulary buys describes a tokenizer nobody has trained and cannot be measured until somebody does.

vocab_trade.costs.value.source: derived from the projection arithmetic in docs/DECISIONS.md 4.4

vocab_trade.buys.value.source: THE ONE UNMEASURED INPUT: an assumption about a candidate tokenizer that has never been trained. Everything else in this record follows from it.

vocab_trade.over.value.source: the India share of the shipping mixture, recomputed on every export

vocab_trade.steps[].value.source: recomputed on every export by dataframework/vocab_trade.py from the mixture actually shipping

run_cost.steps[].value.source: derived from 6ND, 4.0e14 sustained FLOP/s per H100, and a list hourly rate — see this record's run_cost.note and caveat
